decisions.rationale: Gyarados+Klefki lead: Klefki Prankster Safeguard blocks Venusaur Sleep Powder and Sableye Will-O-Wisp before they act; Gyarados Rain Dance overrides Charizard-Mega-Y Drought, neutering Fire moves and halting Chlorophyll speed. Back: Metagross-Mega (Hammer Arm OHKOs Kingambit, Ice Punch hits Venusaur) and Greninja (Hydro Pump OHKOs Charizard, Ice Beam for Venusaur).
decisions.notebook: Opponent identity = sun (Charizard-Mega-Y Drought + Venusaur Chlorophyll). Gyarados Damp Rock Rain Dance is primary sun override; Klefki Prankster Safeguard blocks Sleep Powder/Will-O-Wisp. In rain: Metagross survives Fire moves, Gyarados takes negligible Fire dmg, Gyarados Stone Edge and Greninja Hydro Pump both OHKO Charizard. Metagross-Mega Hammer Arm guaranteed OHKOs Kingambit. Watch for Raichu Fake Out disrupting setup—Protect through it. Sableye Prankster Taunt can shut Klefki if Sableye outspeeds (Klefki 95 vs Sableye 70-102). Venusaur Focus Sash means it survives one hit. Kingambit Sucker Punch priority threat—Metagross outspeeds and OHKOs first. Tauros-Paldea-Aqua Intimidate can lower Metagross attack but Clear Body pre-Mega blocks it; post-Mega Tough Claws compensates.

decisions.rationale: Lead Mega Charizard Y + Venusaur establishes sun immediately, suppresses Water pressure, and enables Chlorophyll Venusaur. Raichu is the strongest Gyarados/Greninja insurance and speed-control option; Kingambit provides a durable late-game answer into Mega Metagross and Klefki.
decisions.notebook: Primary mode selected: Mega Charizard Y + Chlorophyll Venusaur, with Raichu and Kingambit in back. Opponent roster includes Mega Metagross, Damp Rock Gyarados with Rain Dance, Klefki screens, Expert Belt Protean Greninja, Toxapex, and Snorlax. Preserve sun pressure; Raichu is key versus Water/Flying and Greninja, while Kingambit is the principal late-game Metagross breaker.

selection: Rain Dance (all adjacent, including ally Klefki)
decisions.rationale: Safeguard (Prankster +1) must go up before Venusaur's Chlorophyll-boosted Sleep Powder (200-264 Spe in sun) hits Gyarados. Rain Dance overrides Drought, removing Chlorophyll and weakening Fire. Even if Klefki falls to sun-boosted Heat Wave (87-238%), Safeguard persists 5 turns and Rain Dance still resolves. No other combo guarantees both setups against Venusaur outspeeding Gyarados in sun.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 T1: Led Gyarados+Klefki vs Charizard-Y+Venusaur. Gyarados Intimidate hit both foes (-1 atk). Key speed fact: Venusaur Chlorophyll in sun (200-264) always outspeeds Gyarados (124), so Safeguard MUST go up before Rain Dance to block Sleep Powder. Safeguard persists after user faints. Klefki is fragile to sun Heat Wave (87-238%, possible OHKO). Plan: T1 Rain Dance+Safeguard; if Klefki dies bring Metagross (Mega Evolve next turn). In rain: Metagross survives Fire, Gyarados takes negligible Fire, Stone Edge/Ice Fang hit hard. Venusaur Focus Sash means it survives one hit—need double hit or chip to KO. Watch Raichu Fake Out (Protect through it), Kingambit Sucker Punch (Metagross outspeeds+OHKOs), Sableye Prankster Taunt (Klefki 95 vs Sableye 70-102, Klefki outspeeds).

decisions.rationale: Bring Metagross to Mega Evolve immediately. In rain, Rock Slide hits Charizard-Y 4x SE (spread, both foes) and Ice Punch+Tough Claws handles Venusaur. Metagross is bulky enough to survive in rain while Greninja is frail and vulnerable to opponent's priority users. Safeguard still blocks Sleep Powder for 5 turns.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Gyarados 70% HP, Rain 8 turns, Safeguard 5 turns. Klefki fainted. Metagross incoming to Mega Evolve. Opponent team: Charizard-Y (Timid, 132-167 Spe), Venusaur (Modest, Chlorophyll, Focus Sash, 100-132 Spe in rain), Raichu (Timid, LightningRod, Sitrus, 143-178 Spe, Fake Out), Kingambit (Adamant, Defiant, Life Orb, 70-102 Spe, Sucker Punch), Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (Jolly, Intimidate, Lum, 132-167 Spe), Sableye (Careful, Prankster, Mental Herb, 70-102 Spe). Key: Venusaur Focus Sash needs double-hit or chip to KO. In rain Venusaur slow (no Chlorophyll). Safeguard blocks Sleep Powder 5 turns. Gyarados immune to Ground (Scorching Sands, Earth Power). Watch Raichu Fake Out on Metagross switch-in—Protect through it. Kingambit Sucker Punch threatens—Metagross outspeeds and Hammer Arm OHKOs. Sableye Prankster Taunt/Quash slower than Klefki was. Plan: T2 Mega Metagross Rock Slide both foes (4x Charizard), Gyarados Ice Fang Venusaur to break Sash.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve for immediate sun and Chlorophyll. Sleep Powder pressures the Damp Rock Rain Dance line unless Klefki commits Safeguard; if it instead sets a screen, Gyarados is disabled. Heat Wave maximizes simultaneous pressure on Klefki and meaningful chip on Gyarados.
decisions.notebook: Core plan: use Mega Charizard Y sun to enable Chlorophyll Venusaur. Against Damp Rock Gyarados plus Klefki, prioritize denying or punishing Rain Dance: Sleep Powder Gyarados is strong when Klefki chooses a screen, while pressure on Klefki punishes Safeguard. Raichu is the key reserve into Water/Flying and Greninja; preserve Kingambit to threaten Mega Metagross late. Gyarados carries Stone Edge and can heavily punish Charizard, so do not leave Charizard exposed unnecessarily once sun value is obtained.

decisions.rationale: Stone Edge guaranteed OHKOs Charizard-Y (101.6-235.3%, 80% acc). Rock Slide backs up on Charizard (4x, 67-151.6%) and chips Venusaur (15.5-36.1%), neutralizing Focus Sash since Venusaur lacks recovery. Mega Evo boosts Metagross to 130-162 Spe and better bulk. Rock Slide's spread coverage handles Protect mindgames better than single-target Ice Punch. Double Ground on Metagross (80.7-140.3%) is the main risk but requires both foes to commit and not Protect.
decisions.notebook: Key calcs: Gyarados Stone Edge = guaranteed OHKO on Charizard-Y (4x, 101.6-235.3%, 80% acc). Mega Metagross Rock Slide = 67-151.6% Charizard (4x spread), 15.5-36.1% Venusaur (neutral spread). Ice Punch Venusaur = 41.7-96.8% (2x Tough Claws). Ice Fang Venusaur = 32.1-73.5% (2x). Scorching Sands on Mega Metagross = 43.3-72.5%. EarthPower = 37.4-67.8%. Double Ground = 80.7-140.3% (potential KO from 100%). Heat Wave rain on Mega Metagross = 31.6-53.8% (survivable). Mega Metagross Spe 130-162 overlaps Charizard 132-167. Venusaur 100-132 in rain (slow, no Chlorophyll). Focus Sash neutralized by any damage <100% HP since Venusaur has no recovery and Sash only works at full HP. Plan: T2 KO Charizard with Stone Edge + Rock Slide backup, chip Venusaur. T3 finish Venusaur with Ice Punch or Rock Slide. Watch for Raichu Fake Out or Tauros Intimidate on incoming switch after Charizard KO. Safeguard 4 turns blocks Sleep Powder. Gyarados immune to Ground, resists Fire in rain.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Double-target Mega Metagross with the strongest immediate Ground pressure. Scorching Sands plus Earth Power can combine for a KO range while Venusaur’s Focus Sash cushions an Ice Punch; leaving Metagross unchecked is more dangerous than trying to interact with Gyarados through rain.
decisions.notebook: Opponent revealed Damp Rock Gyarados with Stone Edge, Ice Fang, Protect, Rain Dance and Intimidate; it can reset rain and strongly threatens Mega Charizard Y. Klefki showed Safeguard, Light Screen, Reflect, Protect with Light Clay and is fainted. Metagross is Adamant Metagrossite with Protect, Rock Slide, Ice Punch, Hammer Arm; prioritize Ground pressure and preserve Kingambit for it when feasible. Greninja is Timid Expert Belt Protean with Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Dark Pulse, Protect. Toxapex is Bold Leftovers Regenerator with Baneful Bunker, Haze, Recover, Chilling Water. Snorlax is Careful Sitrus Thick Fat with Protect, Body Slam, Brick Break, Yawn. Raichu is the key Electric pressure into Gyarados/Greninja and Lightning Rod utility; preserve it where possible. Safeguard blocks Sleep Powder while active.

decisions.rationale: Raichu is the strongest replacement: it immediately pressures the revealed Gyarados with Electric STAB while retaining Lightning Rod utility against future opposing Electric coverage. Kingambit is poorly positioned into Gyarados and is more valuable for the remaining Psychic- and Ghost-vulnerable threats.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Gyarados is Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate with Protect, Stone Edge, Ice Fang, and Rain Dance; it can reset rain and threatens Fire/Flying Pokémon. Klefki was Light Clay Prankster with screens and Safeguard. Mega Metagross was Adamant with Protect, Rock Slide, Ice Punch, Hammer Arm; it is no longer a concern this game. Greninja is Timid Expert Belt Protean with Protect, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Dark Pulse. Toxapex is Bold Leftovers Regenerator with Baneful Bunker, Haze, Recover, Chilling Water. Snorlax is Careful Sitrus Thick Fat with Protect, Body Slam, Brick Break, Yawn. Preserve Raichu when feasible for Electric pressure into Water/Flying foes and Lightning Rod utility; preserve Kingambit for favorable late-game Dark/Steel matchups. Safeguard blocks Sleep Powder while active.

decisions.rationale: Protect Gyarados to block Raichu's guaranteed 4x Thunderbolt KO (92-174% at 70% HP). Greninja Hydro Pumps Raichu (59.9-140.7%, possible OHKO, 80% acc, rain-boosted). If Raichu Thunderbolts into Protect, we get a free attack. If Raichu Fake Outs Greninja instead, Gyarados is safe and Fake Out is consumed. Removing Raichu eliminates the only guaranteed KO threat to Gyarados, letting us safely double-target Venusaur next turn to break Sash + KO. Gyarados can't switch (both others fainted), so keeping it alive is critical.
decisions.notebook: Raichu Thunderbolt = guaranteed KO on Gyarados at 70% HP (92.3-173.6% max HP, 4x SE). Greninja Hydro Pump on Raichu: 59.9-140.7% (possible OHKO, 80% acc, rain-boosted, neutral). Gyarados Stone Edge on Raichu: 34.1-87.4% (no OHKO). Greninja Dark Pulse on Raichu: 29.3-68.9%. Combined Hydro Pump + Stone Edge = guaranteed KO if both hit. Venusaur Earth Power on Greninja: 26.5-49% (survivable). Greninja Ice Beam on Venusaur: 41.2-89.7% (breaks Sash, no OHKO). Gyarados Ice Fang on Venusaur: 32.1-73.5%. Combined Ice Beam + Ice Fang = 73.3-163.2% (guaranteed KO through Sash if both hit). Speed: Greninja 189 > Raichu 143-178 > Gyarados 124 > Venusaur 100-132. Gyarados cannot switch (Metagross+Klefki fainted). Safeguard 3 turns blocks Sleep Powder. Venusaur used Earth Power T2 so can Protect T3 but not consecutively after. Plan: KO Raichu first (removes 4x Thunderbolt threat to Gyarados), then double-target Venusaur to break Sash + KO. Opponent bench: Kingambit (Life Orb, Defiant, 70-102 Spe), Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (Lum Berry, Intimidate, 132-167 Spe), Sableye (Mental Herb, Prankster, 70-102 Spe).

decisions.rationale: Thunderbolt is a guaranteed KO on the revealed 69% Gyarados if Raichu acts, removing the rain setter and its dangerous Water/Flying pressure. Venusaur Protect denies Greninja’s Ice Beam and Gyarados’s Ice Fang this turn, preserving it for the Greninja endgame while avoiding ineffective Sleep Powder through Safeguard.
decisions.notebook: Gyarados is Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate with Protect, Stone Edge, Ice Fang, Rain Dance; prioritize removing it with Raichu Electric attacks. Greninja is Timid Expert Belt Protean with Protect, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Dark Pulse; Raichu versus Greninja speed is uncertain, and rain-boosted Hydro Pump can heavily damage or possibly KO Raichu despite Sitrus. Klefki was Light Clay Prankster screens/Safeguard; Mega Metagross was Adamant Protect/Rock Slide/Ice Punch/Hammer Arm. Toxapex and Snorlax remain unbrought possibilities in later games. Safeguard blocks Sleep Powder while active. Preserve Raichu’s Electric pressure and Lightning Rod where possible; Kingambit is the remaining late-game Dark/Steel option.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Gyarados moves after Raichu, so attacking means Gyarados dies to Thunderbolt before it can act. Protect (priority +4) is the only way Gyarados can survive. Combined with Greninja Hydro Pump on Raichu: ~40% Hydro Pump KOs outright, ~13% Hydro Pump hits+Protect succeeds (finish Raichu next turn), ~7% Hydro Pump misses+Protect succeeds. ~60% Gyarados survival vs ~40% if attacking. If Gyarados dies, Greninja is 1v2 and likely loses.
decisions.notebook: Raichu has NO Protect (moves: FakeOut/Thunderbolt/Electroweb/Encore). Fake Out fails after turn 1 on field. Gyarados moves after Raichu (124 vs 143-178), so any Gyarados attack is mooted if Raichu Thunderbolts first — only Protect (pri +4) saves it. Double-targeting Raichu with both attacks does NOT guarantee KO because Gyarados faints before attacking if Raichu uses Thunderbolt. Hydro Pump alone on Raichu: 59.9-140.7% rain-boosted, ~50% OHKO chance at 80% acc. Plan if Raichu KO'd T4: double-target Venusaur T5 (Ice Beam+Ice Fang=guaranteed KO through Sash) while Safeguard still up (1 turn left T5). Safeguard expires T6. Opponent bench: Kingambit (LO, Defiant, 70-102 Spe), Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (LumBerry, Intimidate, 132-167 Spe), Sableye (MentalHerb, Prankster, 70-102 Spe). Tauros Intimidate could cut Gyarados attack on entry.

decisions.rationale: Thunderbolt is a guaranteed KO on Gyarados at its shown HP if it does not successfully Protect. Earth Power is Venusaur’s only immediate damaging option into Greninja in rain; Solar Beam would require charging, while Sleep Powder remains blocked by Safeguard.
decisions.notebook: Gyarados: Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate, Protect/Stone Edge/Ice Fang/Rain Dance. Greninja: Timid Expert Belt Protean, Protect/Hydro Pump/Ice Beam/Dark Pulse; Raichu-Greninja Speed order is EV-dependent. Rain-boosted Hydro Pump can possibly OHKO Raichu, while Ice Beam is dangerous to Venusaur. Klefki: Light Clay Prankster screens/Safeguard. Mega Metagross: Adamant Protect/Rock Slide/Ice Punch/Hammer Arm. Preserve Raichu’s Electric pressure and Lightning Rod where possible; Kingambit is the remaining late-game Dark/Steel option. Toxapex and Snorlax were not brought and remain later-game possibilities.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Double-target Venusaur with Ice Beam+Ice Fang to KO through Focus Sash while Safeguard blocks Sleep Powder. Ice Beam (41-90%) breaks Sash, Ice Fang (32-74%) finishes. Sucker Punch can't KO Greninja (19-54% vs 59% HP). Even if Gyarados falls to Sucker Punch, Ice Beam still breaks Sash and Greninja KOs Venusaur next turn. Safeguard expires T6 so we must act now.
decisions.notebook: Raichu has NO Protect (FakeOut/Thunderbolt/Electroweb/Encore). Venusaur: FocusSash, Chlorophyll, Modest, 100-132 Spe, moves SleepPowder/SolarBeam/EarthPower/Protect. Kingambit: LifeOrb, Defiant, Adamant, 70-102 Spe, moves KowtowCleave/IronHead/SuckerPunch/Protect. Sucker Punch max 77% on Gyarados (can KO at 70% HP on high roll), max 54% on Greninja (safe at 59%). Opponent bench: Tauros-Paldea-Aqua (LumBerry/Intimidate/132-167 Spe), Sableye (MentalHerb/Prankster/70-102 Spe). Tauros Intimidate cuts Gyarados attack on entry. If Venusaur KO'd T5, next threat is Kingambit+bench; Greninja Hydro Pump is only neutral option vs Kingambit. Plan T6+: if Venusaur dead, focus Kingambit with Hydro Pump; watch for Sucker Punch mind games.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur Protect prevents the obvious Ice Beam/Ice Fang double-up while Safeguard is still active. Life Orb Sucker Punch into attacking Gyarados deals 40.6–74.1%, giving a real KO chance from its shown damage and forcing its unreliable third Protect; targeting Greninja only deals 12.3–23.8% while resisted.
decisions.notebook: Gyarados: Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate; Protect/Stone Edge/Ice Fang/Rain Dance. Greninja: Timid Expert Belt Protean; Protect/Hydro Pump/Ice Beam/Dark Pulse. Klefki: Light Clay Prankster; Light Screen/Safeguard/Reflect/Protect. Mega Metagross: Adamant; Protect/Rock Slide/Ice Punch/Hammer Arm. Toxapex and Snorlax were not brought in game 1. In rain, preserve Venusaur with Protect/Focus Sash where possible against Ice Beam plus Ice Fang; Solar Beam requires a charge in rain. Kingambit's Life Orb Sucker Punch is strong neutral pressure on Gyarados but resisted by Water/Dark Greninja. Protean type changes should be tracked after each Greninja attack.

decisions.rationale: Gyarados at 8% must Protect—Sucker Punch KOs it (19-64% neutral). Greninja Ice Beams Venusaur for 34-75% (SE, 100% acc), dropping it to 25-66% HP; Focus Sash never triggers since Ice Beam can't OHKO from full. Next turn, double-target Venusaur: min combined Ice Beam+Ice Fang (66.3%) always exceeds max remaining HP (65.8%), guaranteeing KO. Opponent can't switch (only 2 mons left). Risk: Venusaur Sleep Powder on Greninja (75% acc), but Gyarados alive as backup attacker next turn.
decisions.notebook: Ice Beam on Venusaur: 34-75% (SE 2x, 100% acc). Never OHKOs from 100%, Focus Sash stays inactive. Ice Fang on Venusaur: 32-74% (SE 2x). Combined Ice Beam+Ice Fang: 66-148%, ALWAYS KOs Venusaur if at ≤66% HP (min combined 66.3% > max remaining 65.8%). Sucker Punch on Gyarados: 19-64% neutral, KOs at 8%. Tools use Greninja base type (Water/Dark) for Dark moves=NVE 0.5x, but Protean makes Greninja Ice-typed; Dark vs Ice=neutral 1x, so real Sucker Punch on Greninja ~24-83%, can KO at 59% (~40% chance). Venusaur Protect used T3+T5; 3rd use=25% success, 4th=12.5%. Sleep Powder=75% acc in rain (no reduction). Opponent CANNOT switch in game 1: only Venusaur+Kingambit remain. Plan T7: double-target Venusaur for guaranteed KO. If Greninja asleep, Gyarados Ice Fang alone may not KO (32-74% vs 25-66% remaining). Sucker Punch mind games on Gyarados continue—consider Protect bait if opponent expects attack. Kingambit Life Orb recoil on connecting hits only.

decisions.rationale: Sucker Punch acts before Gyarados and guarantees its removal if it attacks; Earth Power then gives reliable immediate damage into Greninja after its Ice Beam. This avoids relying on Sleep Powder accuracy and prevents Gyarados from combining Ice Fang with Greninja’s Ice Beam.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 revealed opponent sets: Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate Gyarados (Protect/Stone Edge/Ice Fang/Rain Dance); Timid Expert Belt Protean Greninja (Protect/Hydro Pump/Ice Beam/Dark Pulse); Bold Light Clay Prankster Klefki; Adamant Mega Metagross. Toxapex and Snorlax were not brought. Track Greninja’s Protean type after each attack. In rain, Solar Beam requires charging. Venusaur’s Focus Sash is valuable against Ice pressure; Kingambit’s priority is key for finishing faster threats.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Venusaur: both Ice Fang and Ice Beam are guaranteed KOs at 23%. Kingambit can only Sucker Punch one of us—the other still KOs Venusaur. Only Venusaur Protect (25% success on 3rd use) saves it. If Kingambit uses any non-Sucker Punch move, both outspeed and Venusaur falls, keeping 2v1. Alternatives risk Sucker Punch on the sole attacker, leaving Venusaur alive with Sleep Powder. Hydro Pump does 32-69% to Kingambit if Greninja survives the 1v1.
decisions.notebook: Sucker Punch on Greninja: tool shows 11.7-41.5% NVE (uses base Water/Dark), but Protean→Ice-type when selecting Ice Beam makes Dark neutral (1x), real ~24-83%, guaranteed KO at 15%. Sucker Punch on Gyarados: 19-64%, guaranteed KO at 8%. Both Ice Beam (34-75%) and Ice Fang (32-74%) guaranteed KO Venusaur at ≤23%. Venusaur Protect T3+T5 used; 3rd use=25%, 4th=12.5%. Hydro Pump on Kingambit: 32-69% neutral, cannot OHKO from 90%. Kingambit Life Orb recoil ~10% per connecting hit. Kingambit Sucker Punch (+1 priority) always outspeeds Greninja's Hydro Pump in 1v1 mind games. Opponent CANNOT switch in game 1. Game 2: opponent brings 4 of {Charizard-Y, Venusaur, Raichu, Kingambit, Tauros-Aqua, Sableye}; expect Sableye (Prankster Taunt/Quash/WillOWisp) and Tauros-Aqua (Intimidate+AquaJet) as likely additions. Klefki screens+Safeguard valuable vs Sleep Powder+status. Metagross-Mega weak to Fire/Ground on sun team—consider leading differently.

decisions.rationale: Protect Venusaur from Greninja’s guaranteed Ice Beam KO while Sucker Punch pressures the 7% Gyarados before it can act. Gyarados’s next Protect has reduced success, so this creates a strong immediate removal chance; targeting Greninja instead invites its first-use Protect with no progress.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 revealed opponent sets: Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate Gyarados (Protect/Stone Edge/Ice Fang/Rain Dance); Timid Expert Belt Protean Greninja (Protect/Hydro Pump/Ice Beam/Dark Pulse); Bold Light Clay Prankster Klefki; Adamant Mega Metagross. Toxapex and Snorlax were not brought. Track Greninja’s Protean type after each attack. In rain, Solar Beam requires charging. Venusaur’s Focus Sash remains valuable against Ice pressure; Kingambit’s priority is key for finishing faster threats.

decisions.rationale: Greninja is my last Pokémon at 15% HP. Kingambit's Sucker Punch (+1 priority) does 25-47% even NVE, guaranteed KO at 15%, and resolves before any attacking move. Even if I Protect to survive this turn, any hit next turn KOs me (Kowtow Cleave NVE 40%+, Iron Head NVE 37%+). No path to victory exists; forfeiting saves time for games 2-3.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lost. Opponent brought Charizard-Y/Venusaur/Raichu/Kingambit. Key sets: Charizard-Y Timid 132-167 Spe; Venusaur Modest FocusSash Chlorophyll 100-132 Spe (SleepPowder/SolarBeam/EarthPower/Protect); Raichu Timid Sitrus LightningRod 143-178; Kingambit Adamant LifeOrb Defiant 70-102 (SuckerPunch+1/KowtowCleave/IronHead/Protect). Kingambit SuckerPunch KOs Greninja at 15% even NVE via Protean Dark-type. Game 2: expect Sableye (Prankster Taunt/Quash/Wisp) + Tauros-Aqua (Intimidate+AquaJet) as likely additions. DO NOT lead Metagross into sun team (weak to Fire/Ground). Klefki screens+Safeguard critical vs Sleep Powder/status. Consider Klefki+Gyarados or Klefki+Greninja lead. Gyarados Intimidate valuable but watch SuckerPunch mind games. Greninja ExpertBelt Protean best vs Venusaur (IceBeam 45-82%). HydroPump neutral on Kingambit 32-69% cannot OHKO from 80%.

decisions.rationale: Life Orb Sucker Punch is a guaranteed KO on the revealed 14% Greninja if it uses an attacking move; Earth Power is the best backup if Sucker Punch fails against a non-attacking choice. Greninja’s only realistic escape is Protect.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 opponent reveals: Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate Gyarados (Protect/Stone Edge/Ice Fang/Rain Dance); Timid Expert Belt Protean Greninja (Protect/Hydro Pump/Ice Beam/Dark Pulse); Bold Light Clay Prankster Klefki (Light Screen/Safeguard/Reflect/Protect); Adamant Mega Metagross (Protect/Rock Slide/Ice Punch/Hammer Arm). Toxapex and Snorlax were not brought. Track Greninja’s Protean type after attacks. In rain, Solar Beam requires a charging turn. Venusaur’s Focus Sash remains valuable against Ice pressure; Kingambit priority is crucial for finishing faster threats.

reflections.summary: Lost because Metagross was brought and Mega Evolved into a sun team where both Charizard-Y's Scorching Sands and Venusaur's Earth Power are super-effective; it fainted turn 2 without acting, wasting the Mega slot. Gyarados traded for Charizard-Y but the remaining three (Gyarados/Klefki/Greninja) couldn't handle Venusaur's Protect stalling plus Kingambit's Sucker Punch cleanup. Klefki provided no value before fainting.
reflections.adjustment: Do not bring Metagross against this Charizard-Y/Venusaur sun core. If Metagross is the only Mega available, consider dropping the Mega entirely and bringing four non-Mega mons with better type matchups—or lead Klefki+Greninja to set screens and pressure Venusaur immediately while keeping Gyarados in reserve for Kingambit/Charizard. Need a cleaner answer to Kingambit Sucker Punch.
reflections.notebook: Game 1 lost. Opponent brought Charizard-Y/Venusaur/Raichu/Kingambit; left out Tauros-Aqua and Sableye. Key sets: Charizard-Y Timid (HeatWave/SolarBeam/ScorchingSands/Protect); Venusaur Modest FocusSash Chlorophyll (SleepPowder/SolarBeam/EarthPower/Protect) — spams Protect under pressure; Raichu Timid Sitrus LightningRod (FakeOut/Tbolt/Electroweb/Encore); Kingambit Adamant LifeOrb Defiant (SuckerPunch/KowtowCleave/IronHead/Protect) — Sucker Punch is the win condition, punishes predictable targeting. Opponent protects to stall and reads Sucker Punch timing well. Game 2: expect Sableye (Prankster Taunt/Quash/Wisp) and/or Tauros-Aqua (Intimidate+AquaJet) as likely swaps in. Metagross is dead weight vs sun (4x weak to Fire, 2x weak to Ground from both Charizard-Y and Venusaur). Klefki screens+Safeguard still critical vs Sleep Powder but must accomplish something before fainting. Greninja ExpertBelt Ice Beam is the best Venusaur answer (2HKO through sash). Gyarados Stone Edge OHKOed Charizard-Y — keep as Charizard answer but protect from Sucker Punch. Consider not Mega Evolving at all if Metagross is only option; bring Greninja+Gyarados+Klefki+fourth with better Kingambit matchup.

reflections.summary: Won because the Charizard-Y/Venusaur bring immediately removed Mega Metagross, then Venusaur plus Kingambit’s Protect and Sucker Punch endgame outlasted Gyarados and left Greninja in range. The preview plan was sound: Mega Charizard Y was the right evolution to pressure Metagross, though it was exposed to Gyarados Stone Edge.
reflections.adjustment: For game 2, consider preserving Charizard more carefully against the revealed Stone Edge Gyarados—lead or position Raichu to threaten it first—while retaining Kingambit/Venusaur as the rain-endgame core. Do not rely on Solar Beam once Gyarados has established rain.
reflections.notebook: Opponent Game 1: Gyarados is Jolly Damp Rock Intimidate with Protect, Stone Edge, Ice Fang, Rain Dance; it can overwrite sun and directly threaten Mega Charizard Y. Greninja is Timid Expert Belt Protean with Protect, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Dark Pulse; Ice Beam pressures Venusaur, and Protean typing should be tracked. Klefki is Bold Light Clay Prankster with Light Screen, Safeguard, Reflect, Protect. Mega Metagross is Adamant with Protect, Rock Slide, Ice Punch, Hammer Arm and is vulnerable to Charizard-Y/Venusaur Ground pressure. Toxapex and Snorlax were omitted in Game 1. Future plan: Charizard-Y/Venusaur is a viable anti-Metagross mode, but pair/position Raichu to deter Gyarados before committing Charizard; preserve Kingambit priority for Greninja/Gyarados endgames; avoid Solar Beam under rain.
